f.title: Inform the Authority of ADR reports within 7 days and keep them open to inspection
f.statement: Under the Standard Provisions for Product Licence, the licence holder shall inform the Authority within 7 days of receiving any report it is aware of on adverse effects in humans or animals associated with use of a licensed medicinal product; such reports are open to inspection by persons authorised by the Authority, who may take copies, and if directed the holder shall furnish the Authority with a copy of any such report it holds or becomes aware of. The guideline adds that, in line with these Medicines Regulations, the product licence holder is legally obligated to report ADRs to the BDMCA.
f.legal_basis: Medicines (Licensing, Standard Provisions and Fees) Regulations 2010, First Schedule, Regulation 4

rows.actor: Product licence holder
rows.deadline: Within 7 days upon receipt of the report
rows.quote:
"The holder of the licence shall inform the Authority within 7 days upon receipt of any
       report of which he is aware of adverse effects in one or more human beings or animals
       associated in that report resulting from the use of any medicinal product to which the
       license relates, which shall be open to inspection by a person authorized by the Authority,
       who may take copies thereof and, if the Authority so directs, the holder of the license shall
       furnish the Authority with a copy of any such report of which he has a record or of which
       he is or subsequently becomes aware".

In line with Brunei Darussalam’s related Medicines Regulations, hence Product License Holder is
legally obligated to report ADRs to the Brunei Darussalam Medicines Control Authority (BDMCA).
rows.review_note: Review: merged row 0002 (the guideline's one-sentence restatement that the product licence holder is legally obligated to report ADRs) into this row, which already carries the binding Regulation 4 duty; quote extended to include that sentence. This is the binding 7-day duty behind the 2.3.1.1 timelines (rows 0012-0013). Penalty provisions (Medicines Order 2007 s77-78) quoted in 2.1 set no step and are not curated. Double-check: confirmed: Regulation 4 standard provision quoted with 'shall inform ... within 7 days'; the guideline's 'legally obligated' sentence supports the actor.

deadline_rule.clock_start: receipt of any report of which he is aware
deadline_rule.applies_to: Reports of adverse effects associated with a licensed medicinal product (legal provision quoted; calendar-day type taken from the guideline's own 7 calendar days for the same duty, Table 1)

f.title: Fatal/life-threatening local ADRs: 24 hours, no later than 7 days; complete report +8 days
f.statement: All serious fatal or life-threatening spontaneous ADRs occurring in Brunei Darussalam should be reported to NADRMC as soon as possible or within 24 hours after first awareness but no later than 7 calendar days; the clock starts when any personnel of the licence holder, including sales representatives, is aware; reports can be sent by e-mail or fax (telephoning NADRMC to ensure receipt); a complete report including an assessment of additional findings should be submitted within 8 additional calendar days from the first report.
f.applicability: Serious fatal or life-threatening spontaneous ADRs occurring in Brunei Darussalam.

rows.actor: Relevant licence holder (product licence holder, licensed manufacturer, wholesaler or importer)
rows.deadline: As soon as possible or within 24 hours after first awareness, no later than 7 calendar days; complete report within 8 additional calendar days after the first report; clock starts when any licence-holder personnel, including sales representatives, is aware
rows.quote:
All serious fatal or life-threatening spontaneous ADR reports occurring in Brunei
       Darussalam that arise from the use of the medicinal product should be reported to the
       NADRMC as soon as possible or within 24 hours after first awareness by the relevant
       licence holders but no later than 7 calendar days (Table 1). The clock for reporting starts
       as soon as any personnel of the relevant licence holder, including sales representatives,
       is aware of the ADR (Table 1). The ADR report can be sent by email/ facsimile (telephone
       the NADRMC to ensure receipt of ADR report). A complete report should be submitted
       within 8 additional calendar days from when the first report was submitted (Table 1). This
       report should include an assessment of the additional findings.
rows.review_note: Review: Level kept Recommended: the 2.3.1.1 quote says 'should' and cites Table 1, not the Regulation, so it is decided per quote. The 7-calendar-day outer limit coincides with the binding Regulation 4 duty (First Schedule, Medicines (Licensing, Standard Provisions and Fees) Regulations 2010) captured as Mandatory in row 0001, and 2.3.1 (row 0010) says reports 'must' be submitted within these timelines; the 24-hour target and the 8-day complete report remain guidance. Double-check: confirmed. Below 90: Recommended per the 'should' quote, but 2.3.1 (row 0010) says reports 'must' be submitted within these timelines and Regulation 4 (row 0001) binds the 7 days, so the level is a judgement call.

f.title: State the IBD in each PBRER
f.statement: Each PBRER should state the International Birth Date (first marketing approval of any product with the active substance anywhere); where a report covers different forms, formulations or uses, the earliest approval is the IBD; this determines the DLP.

rows.actor: Relevant licence holder (product licence holder, licensed manufacturer, wholesaler or importer)
rows.quote:

       the date of the first marketing approval for any product containing the active substance
       granted to any company in any country in the world (9). When a report contains
       information on different dosage forms, formulations, or uses (indications, routes and/or
       populations), the date of the first marketing approval for any of the various
       authorisations should be regarded as the IBD (9). This is in order to determine the Data
       Lock Point (DLP) which is the date designated as the cut-off date for data to be included
       in a PBRER (9).
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed. Below 90: the IBD/DLP rationale sentence is explanatory; the IBD basis interacts with the IBD-vs-registration conflict noted at row 0030.

f.statement: A DHPCL should be disseminated when immediate action is needed for a product: new major warnings or precautions; new data on an unknown risk or a change in frequency or severity of a known risk; substantiated reduced efficacy; new recommendations to prevent or treat ADRs or avoid misuse or medication error; or ongoing assessment of an important potential risk with insufficient data for regulatory action.
